Voice and video calls, and voice chats, do not work through an MTProto proxy — that is how the protocol is built, not a fault of this build. Messages, files and voice messages keep working.

Voice and video calls, and voice chats, do not work through an MTProto proxy. This is an architectural limit of MTProto proxies rather than a bug in this app — the original project says the same in its FAQ.

Why
• The proxy carries MTProto over TCP and nothing else.
• A call's audio and video are a separate media stream over UDP (WebRTC), flowing directly between the clients or through Telegram relays. That stream never reaches the proxy, and it cannot be carried over a WebSocket.
• Telegram for Android has no "calls through the proxy" switch at all: the client never hands a call to the proxy. So the proxy does not break calls either — they depend only on whether the phone can reach Telegram's servers directly.

What to do
• In Telegram's proxy settings, turn off "Use proxy for calls" if that option is there.
• Or disable the proxy for the duration of the call: Telegram → Settings → Data and Storage → Proxy → off, then back on afterwards.
• If calls fail without the proxy as well, the network is blocking Telegram calls (the media is UDP). Only a VPN helps there: it carries UDP, an MTProto proxy does not.

How to find out which it is
• Disable the proxy in Telegram and call again: if the call goes through, it is the proxy connection; if it does not, the network is blocking it.
• Diagnostics has a "call path" line that checks whether the phone reaches Telegram directly (TCP only — call media is UDP and cannot be probed this way).
• A log taken during a failed call helps pin the cause down: Logs → Share.

Voice messages, files and video keep working: they go over TCP through the media DC.
